title: Walls, doors and keys
sub: The third film of Locks before the data, the first series of Data protection and privacy: why walls still matter when identity is the boundary, as Ragusa's quarantine law of 1377 kept a trading port open through the plague years; who secures what among the cloud provider, the platform's makers and the university; walls drawn from the map's areas; private paths and a short list of ways out; the catalog as the files' only door; development, test and production kept apart; a key the university holds; and copies nobody can delete.
howto: The film is drawn in the module's look, Night glass: a dark hall of frosted panes, frosted where what's behind may not be read and clear where it may, with cards of near-clear frost and bright rims. Cyan is an identity, green allowed, coral denied or closed, amber power switched on, violet hidden personal data; a key is always a sealed card with a gold chip, never written out. Ragusa in 1377 is painted in the same night light, with its place and year on a tag.
